question.prompt: Approve this implementation contract: Scope—change only `pylint.modify_sys_path()` behavior used by `python -m pylint`/`runpy` and add minimum regression coverage. Required behavior—remove `sys.path[0]` only when its value is exactly `""`, `"."`, or exactly equal to `os.getcwd()`; preserve every other first entry, including paths merely equivalent after normalization, resolution, case conversion, or symlink traversal. When an arbitrary first entry is preserved and `PYTHONPATH` begins or ends with a colon, preserve that arbitrary entry while removing only the applicable exact current-directory entry introduced by the empty PYTHONPATH component. Compatibility—retain the established removals for existing exact-empty-string/current-working-directory cases, retain explicit-current-directory PYTHONPATH exceptions, and retain trailing working-directory entries used by editable installations. Acceptance—tests must prove an arbitrary prefix survives, the applicable following exact cwd entry is removed under leading/trailing-colon handling, and existing covered path-stripping/plugin-import behavior remains passing. Exclusions—no changes to console-script behavior, path normalization/equivalence matching, unrelated import handling, supported environments, or public APIs. Implementation discretion—internal control flow and exact test fixture organization may vary, provided removals are value-qualified, safe for the exercised path shapes, and all acceptance checks pass. Residual risk—uncited unusual `sys.path` layouts may retain entries that are cwd-equivalent but not one of the approved exact values; this is intentionally accepted to avoid broader deletion behavior. Is this contract approved for implementation?
